title: Quick Sort Partition
statement: Partition an array around a pivot element.
inputOutputContract: Partition using the last value as pivot and the Lomuto algorithm (scan j=0..n-2; swap when a[j]<=pivot; place pivot at i+1). Output the EXACT resulting array, not fully sorted.

mistakes.hint1: Inspect the uses first element as pivot behavior in partition; the current algorithm is close, but one operation changes its result.
mistakes.hint2: Start by tracing T1 manually. Watch array indices / comparisons / loop boundaries / return values at each iteration or recursive return.
mistakes.hint3: Check the invariant of partition: Lomuto partition uses the last element as pivot, inclusive <= comparison, and a final pivot swap.
mistakes.hint4: Concentrate on the expression or branch that controls this mistake: `int pivot = arr[0]`. What does it do on the failing input?
mistakes.hint5: Compare the intermediate state with the expected output of T1. The mistake is in uses first element as pivot, not merely formatting.
mistakes.hint6: Adjust the faulty operation so that it follows this rule: Lomuto partition uses the last element as pivot, inclusive <= comparison, and a final pivot swap.
mistakes.hint7: A targeted correction is to replace `int pivot = arr[0]` with `int pivot = arr[n - 1]` in partition, then retest T1–T6.
